newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mint nickel tender attracts low premium.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mint nickel tender attracts low premium.

text.p: The U.S. Mint looks set to pick up a bargain 50-tonne parcel of nickel in its latest tender.
The winning seller will almost certainly be Hochschild Partners at a premium of about 7.00 cents a lb over LME cash, seen low by some for such a small amount of metal.
The winning premium nets back to 2 to 3 cents after freight, finance and contango are taken into account, one dealer noted.
The bids were presented after workers at Inco's Sudbury nickel and copper operations went on strike.
Nickel dealers said this week there was no sign of panic among consumers.
"The nickel market is lower now than when the Inco strike was announced. Nobody seems bothered with it. There seems to be plenty of nickel chasing relatively few buyers," a dealer said.
A merchant added: "I certainly don't believe anyone thinks this will be a long strike to the point where they will go out to buy. Why should you panic when you see the nickel price come down?"
